findings.detail: The existing precondition requires argv length >= 3, shell-path equality, argv[1] == -lc, and prepared.command suffix equality. shell_start cannot underflow. Original flag/script replacements occur before the new insertion. Bash receives [original prefix, shell, --norc, -pc, original restore script, original trailing args]. Long option placement precedes -pc. No quoting or shell-string concatenation is added.

ShellType derives Copy in fixed shell_detect.rs; using it after capture and match is legal. The new branch executes only on Bash after successful capture/cache resolution. No new task, child process, ownership transfer, or cancellation path is introduced.

The complete source becomes its original bytes on deleting the seven added lines. Capture -lc, failed-capture early return/fallback -lc, set +o privileged, request/environment policy filtering, prepared prefix, sandbox/permissions, cache key, deadlines/retry budget, and non-Bash handling remain unchanged. This is not --noprofile and does not suppress the separate host-profile noise on fallback.

The complete diagnostic bundle has 10 byte/hash-verified records. Its original JUnit selects exactly the remote_sandbox case and fails its first full tuple: stdout empty, diagnostic stderr identifies .bashrc/line 2/function unset with BASH_ENV empty and the actual restoration string, exit 41. The poison marker has not been reached. This is evidence of pre-restoration profile execution, not a valid cache-key negative and not proof of a specific getpeername syscall or errno.

The fixed positive fixture still has the 8 Unix matrix declarations, plus 3 macOS-only zsh declarations. Both original full output/stderr/status/closed tuples, filtered variables, shadowed builtin controls, in-memory-only/no capture-file assertions and exact sandbox key remain. Original shell_snapshot_tests.rs still has the real bounded/single-flight 3-case retry control and 3 parser tests; no exact -pc vector assertion is invalidated. These statements describe source, not new test passes.

primary_manual.observed: GNU documents the noninteractive remote-shell .bashrc path and that --norc inhibits it.
GNU documents -p suppression of BASH_ENV/ENV and imported shell functions. It is not a documented blanket replacement for --norc.
